summary: Tehama County cabin on a 20 ft steel tower, dated 1939 but preceded by 1916-1920 lookouts on the peak; survived the 2019 South Fire and is listed as standing.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register dates the present lookout to 1939, but a 1916 item and 1920 articles describe a Forest Service lookout and cabin on the same peak. The sources do not say whether the 1939 structure replaced an earlier one, so the story treats 1939 as the date of the current building.
The 1920 lookout is spelled Brownlee in one article and Bromlee in another; the story uses Brownlee.

notes_for_editor: The 1973 closure rests on a single visitor's comment on the NHLR page, so it is marked as one account. The 6.1 m height is the 20 ft tower alone, per the NHLR description. Current access is not documented in any source read; the 1973 'long, dusty dirt road' comment is historical and not used as current access. A web search summary mentioned a 2015 trip report describing the lookout as locked and shuttered; it was not fetched and is not used. Wikipedia's Tomhead Mountain article has no lookout history. The only survival source is the NHLR page; no second source for the South Fire damage was found.
